title: Trapping Rain Water
prompt: Write a Python function `trap(height: list[int]) -> int` that computes how much rain water is trapped after raining, given an elevation map where each element is the height of a bar of width 1. Return 0 if no water is trapped or if the input is empty.

title: Course Schedule (Cycle Detection)
prompt: Write a Python function `can_finish(num_courses: int, prerequisites: list[list[int]]) -> bool` that returns True if all courses can be finished. Each prerequisite `[a, b]` means course `b` must be taken before course `a`. Return False if the prerequisites contain a cycle that makes completion impossible.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
prompt: Write a Python function `longest_palindrome(s: str) -> str` that returns the longest palindromic substring of `s`. If several palindromic substrings share the maximum length, return the one with the smallest starting index. Return an empty string if `s` is empty.

title: Daily Temperatures
prompt: Write a Python function `daily_temperatures(temperatures: list[int]) -> list[int]` that returns a list `answer` where `answer[i]` is the number of days to wait after day `i` for a warmer temperature. If there is no warmer day in the future, `answer[i]` is 0.

title: Word Search in Grid
prompt: Write a Python function `exist(board: list[list[str]], word: str) -> bool` that returns True if `word` can be constructed from sequentially adjacent cells (up, down, left, right) of `board`, where each cell may be used at most once. The word is non-empty.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
prompt: Write a Python function `can_partition(nums: list[int]) -> bool` that returns True if `nums` can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sums. Return True if `nums` is empty (both subsets are empty).

title: Merge K Sorted Linked Lists
prompt: Define a `ListNode` class with `val` and `next` attributes. Write a Python function `merge_k_lists(lists: list) -> object` that merges `k` sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list and returns its head. An empty input list, or a list containing only `None`, must return `None`.
test_cases: for v in vals[1:]: c.next=ListNode(v); c=c.next

title: Decode Nested String
prompt: Write a Python function `decode_string(s: str) -> str` that decodes an encoded string. The encoding rule is `k[encoded_string]`, where `encoded_string` is repeated exactly `k` times; `k` is a positive integer that may have multiple digits, and encodings may be nested. Plain letters outside brackets are kept as-is.

title: Unique Permutations
prompt: Write a Python function `permute_unique(nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]` that returns all unique permutations of `nums` (which may contain duplicates), sorted in lexicographical order. For an empty input, return `[[]]`.

title: Jump Game II (Minimum Jumps)
prompt: Write a Python function `jump(nums: list[int]) -> int` that returns the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the last index, where `nums[i]` is the maximum jump length from index `i`. Return -1 if the last index cannot be reached, and 0 if `nums` has 0 or 1 element.
